title: Introduction: Why this isn't a poker book
heading: Introduction: Why this isn't a poker book
coreClaim: The introduction reframes the book as a guide to better decisions under uncertainty rather than as a poker memoir, and it opens by separating outcome quality from decision quality.
distinctMechanism: The chapter uses a famous failed football play to expose resulting, then uses the poker-versus-chess contrast to explain why hidden information and luck make hindsight judgment unreliable.
requiredAnchors: Pete Carroll's goal-line pass call in Super Bowl XLIX as the opening resulting case.
Poker versus chess as the core contrast between incomplete and near-complete information.
Calibrated uncertainty as a stronger stance than false certainty.
commonMisreadings: Uncertainty means outcomes do not matter.
Poker is just branding rather than the structural analogy for the whole book.
specificApplications: Judge decisions by the information available when the choice was made.
Express beliefs in calibrated confidence terms.
Use later chapters as tools for better process, not for guaranteed outcomes.
hardEdgeRequirement: Keep humility and accountability in tension. The chapter cannot let uncertainty collapse into excuse-making.
thresholdQuestion: If the scoreboard is noisy, how should a serious person judge a choice?
